key_insight: Closed-loop control using infrared thermography can stabilize continuous ultrasonic welding of CFRPs by using measured surface temperature as the feedback reference.
engineering_relevance: This approach could improve weld-seam robustness and repeatability in high-rate aerospace composite joining where boundary conditions change continuously.
method: Use an infrared camera to measure temperature during welding.
Feed temperature back to the controller as the process reference variable.
Compare against constant-amplitude and constant-power control.
evidence_signal: Preliminary results were evaluated with destructive and non-destructive testing and indicate improved process robustness and repeatability over conventional control methods.
watch_item: As a short preliminary study, the method still needs deeper validation across more materials, seam geometries, and production conditions before broad deployment.
paper_title: Introducing a Novel Infrared-Thermography-Based Control Method for Continuous Ultrasonic Welding of CFRPs
